commenti.body:
I don’t know but it completely fucked the career of an incredibly talented director. Hopefully the parties involved have done a retrospective and put in place guardrails to make sure nothing like this happens again.

Iirc, Scorsese was an executive producer, too.
Scorsese was even originally going to direct it.

It's reasons like this why I think every film should invest in having a documentarian follow along for the story of production.  In such a failure when the movie never really comes to fruition, the documentary may prove to be a viable economic rejoinder as a look into how catastrophic the filmmaking process can be.  And, in the event the movie turns out mediocre or great, the documentary footage can go to support behind the scenes accessories to the movie.

I don’t know what you’re talking about. In our house, the Academy Award winning Snowman (animated short, 1982) with the stellar soundtrack is on regular rotation every Christmas season in our house.
I mean, I think they do generally, even the low-budget shoots I’ve been involved in had people capturing BTS. I suppose how much they document would vary but it’s normal practice.
In your house, it's on rotation in your house? In my opinion, that's pretty cool in my opinion.
The Snowman is playing at their house, THEIR house...
[removed]

incidentally, i think it was alfredson's star power that screwed the project. a lot of pressure and expectation was on him to turn out a masterpiece like he previous two films, but it sounds like he simply didn't have enough time, or wasn't forceful enough to demand the time, or perhaps he wasn't in the position to turn it down. but he should've. because a film doesn't get fucked like that unless serious mistakes are made at the highest levels of the production.

If you Google, you’ll find the story of how the Director just didn’t film 20 pages (ish) of script. I’m pretty sure it was down to money and he just gave up.

The podcast “how did this get made“ also has a good episode that specifically addresses the absurdity of the whole thing.

Clearly a lot of the script didn't get shot. There have been a lot of rumors about certain above the line talent causing production issues on that movie. I don't usually put a lot of stock in that type of gossip, but it is noticeable that the person was tipped for A list stardom and is now a B list at best.
The editing is credited to Thelma Schoonmaker and Claire Simpson. There's 3 BAFTAs and 4 Oscars between them. Whatever happened during production, the footage clearly wasn't there to save it.
Who is that? I wonder if this is the person Rebecca Ferguson was talking about.

By process of elimination, I'm pretty sure it has to be the person she called out, no matter what got said on the press tour. 

https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/michael-fassbender-abuse-allegations-sunawin-leasi-andrews-1201927946/

Saw the film out of morbid curiosity and… yeah, it was pretty much as bad as they say.

I haven’t read the novel it was based on but, at least trying to figure out things that weren’t filmed here and there, the story might just be one of those things that works better as a novel versus a film.  There were just too many weird diversions/red herrings and characters that, again, might have been more fleshed out in the book versus the (admittedly not completely filmed) movie.

As others have mentioned, supposedly there were chunks of the script which weren’t filmed and *by the Gods* does it show.  Val Kilmer was clearly *very* ill during the filming and having him voiced over was odd, to say the least.

The only good thing I can say about the film is that it looked quite beautiful.

Otherwise… what a disaster.
It really is tragic, the novel is one of the best thrillers I've read. Stayed up all night to finish it. I was so excited about the film adaptation and ended up not even seeing it on Netflix.
Fassbender would be the only person this applies to. I would consider him higher than “B-list at best” personally. Fassbender is strongly believed to be the culprit though.

There is a fantastic video on the subject by the YouTube channel Folding Ideas. I highly recommend it!.

Dan Olson describes what editing is and how the lack in quality thereof is the main reason the film feels wonky. It was obviously unfinished and rushed out.
How's that even possible? As a director how out of touch can you be with your material that you don't realize you miss that much of footage?! It is amazingly incompetent.
Nah, there are lots of photos of Ferguson laughing and joking with Fassbender on this set, she's close with Vikander, and straight after this shoot she went on a vacation with the two of them.

That is completely bs, Rebecca has literally said that she like working with him and there are plenty of videos of them getting along.

It's most likely Hugh Grant because he was in the news last year about yelling at a female co-worker.

There has not been a lot rumors at all that imply any of that, source please.

Yep, great video!
One can imagine what a nightmare of a movie could come out of it, if less skilled editors managed the available footage.
Fair enough. I wasn’t aware of that. Just going off bullshit I read.

I must’ve accidentally edited that out. It’s “how did this get made“.
What's kind of brilliant is that you also originally left out 20% of the information in your comment Perhaps any engagement with this material causes, wait, what's it called again...?
Like Lost in La Mancha.

I sorta don’t believe it. Granted I work in television and movies are run a tad differently. Scheduling is a huge expense to get everything ready before filming even starts. In preproduction you have hundreds of meetings with tons of departments planning a million different things. *Someone* would’ve brought up the fact that stuff wasn’t going to be filmed that was scheduled to be filmed.

It could be a cover story for something else, but isn't admitting that you forgot to shoot scenes basically a career suicide? Would you work with this person on any production after hearing this story? I feel like you would create a better lie to protect yourself, but then why would you even admit it if it is true. Such a confusing situation.

Seeing this in the theater was a memorable experience.

The longer it went on the more confused the audience was. It was palpable. You could feel it. Around the time of the unceremonious and uncommented in death of a main character, the tenor turned to angry. Someone went and got an usher and made them stand in the back and watch. And then around the time of the weird dry humping sex scene, the feeling turned to some sort of weird fever-dream-adjacent mania and people were laughing and enjoying themselves again.

When it ended and we walked out, it was like we'd all experienced something momentous together.

It was, super super weird.

Yes, missing roughly 20% of the plot is obviously a huge problem. But a lot of what's there doesn't make sense even in a "with the scene" sense. This film is BAFFLING TO me. 

But there are two heroes of the story and both of them are holes... so...

Plan to shoot in order A. Something happens and you have to reorder to plan B. Then to plan C. By the time you're on plan L you have totally lost the plot on what you needed to go back and pickup and what needs to be done based to changes on the script?

I guess nobody cared about the production, you would expect at least one of the producers would be on top of things. Such a weird situation. And this is a million dollar movie, not a cheap student film.
